summary: Ranger Peak lookout, San Bernardino NF, Riverside County: 1926 cab on an open timber tower, used at Keenwild until 2010; a climbers' log says only pedestal mounts remain.

facts.design: modified L-6 type 8'x8' wood cab on a 20' battered, open timber tower
facts.status_note: The cab was used at the Keenwild helibase until the new operations center opened in 2010. A climbers' log says only the pedestal mounts and rock stairs remain at the summit.
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, San Bernardino National Forest

visit.trail_note: A climbers' log describes a fire road to the summit that careful drivers in passenger cars can use, and a short hike from the highway along an old firebreak. No official source read gives access rules.

events.note: Register: built along with a lookout on Barton Peak to replace the Black Mountain lookout. A climbers' page gives 1935 instead (see notes_for_editor).
The lookout pair served until 1962, when a new structure at Black Mountain replaced them.
Cab removed and stored at the USFS Cranston Fire Station until 1963, then put to use at the newly opened Keenwild Helitack Base.

Per a June 2010 report, the crew built a 560-square-foot office from the dismantled remains of the old lookout, and it was moved uphill in 1974. This conflicts with the register's account of the cab (see notes_for_editor).
Register: the cab was enlarged and modified over time and used until the new Keenwild Helitack Operations Center opened on June 9, 2010.
Registered October 17, 2010, nominated by Brad Eells.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register dates the pair to 1926 and ties the date to the Black Mountain replacement. The SummitPost page says 1935 and gives no basis for it in the lines we read. The story uses 1926 and reports the 1935 claim as a climbers' page's date.

notes_for_editor: Brief note says this record 'shares a register number' with another site. The firelookout.org index table is hard to read from the crawl text, so the match could not be checked; the register's own page gives US 687, CA 10 for Ranger Peak and this record keeps that. Check the other site's record. Unresolved: (1) Cab fate. The register says the cab was enlarged and kept in use until June 2010; Wildfire Today (June 25, 2010) says the crew built a 560-square-foot office from the dismantled remains, moved uphill in 1974. The story reports both. (2) Elevation: the register gives 5,035 ft; SummitPost says 5082 feet (not in the story). (3) Build year: 1926 (register) vs 1935 (SummitPost). The SummitPost page is a climbers' log and its date is not shown in the lines we read; it is the only source for what remains today, so the story presents it as a climber's account. Access: no official source read; the fire road and firebreak details come from the log only. Check San Bernardino NF for closures before relying on the visit note. No staffing or fire history found, so none recorded. Register photos are credited to others and their URLs were not captured; no photos added.
